title: Accessible micro-summary layer for prolonged time-series (ARIA snapshots + DOM pruning)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Long-running time-series (multi-hour streams, high-frequency telemetry) produce very large DOMs when we keep all interactive legend entries, per-point markers, and annotation nodes live. Screen reader users also get overwhelmed by continuous ARIA announcements when the chart updates rapidly. We need a low-overhead, accessible summarization layer that provides informative snapshots and keeps DOM size and reflow low.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Screen-reader users can request a concise ARIA snapshot summary for the visible viewport that contains: series name, latest value, delta over selected window, and any active alerts. 2) The chart renders with a pruned DOM under heavy update load (target: DOM nodes reduced by >=40% vs current) while visual fidelity is preserved. 3) Keyboard-first exploration: tabbing lands on a single micro-summary control per chart that expands to a focused, virtualized list of series. 4) Works with existing theme tokens for color/contrast and spacing; no custom hardcoded values. 5) Perf regression guard: no increase in 99th-percentile frame time for typical synthetic workload (target: <= baseline +5%).
engineering_notes: Implementation approach: 1) Introduce a single 'micro-summary' control per chart (button-like element using design tokens for padding/typography) that toggles an ARIA-live snapshot. 2) Behind the scenes, maintain a lightweight summary model updated on batched intervals (200ms) rather than per-frame. 3) Virtualize legend details: keep only visible series DOM nodes; use an off-DOM cache for metrics used in snapshots. 4) Provide a fallback accessible CSV-export button for users who want full data (reuses table tokens and button component). 5) Coordinate with ENG for KV-cache read patterns to avoid duplicate work. Engineering should add unit and e2e a11y tests (axe, screen-reader snapshots).
notes_on_tokens_and_components: Design token use: rely on core tokens for spacing (space-2/3), typography (body-compact), and color tokens for high-contrast text roles. The micro-summary button should reuse Button/tertiary token set and the compact list should reuse Table/row-height tokens to ensure consistent vertical rhythm. Avoid introducing new color tokens unless product requires a new alert severity color (label and proposal in Figma).
comments: 2026-01-12 - Asha Patel: Initial concept and quick prototype demoed in sync. Demo highlighted 60% fewer DOM nodes in a 10k-point stream when markers and per-point annotations are virtualized.

2026-01-15 - Miguel Ortega (ENG): Reviewed prototype; raised a concern about telemetry read amplification. Suggested moving summary aggregation to the renderer thread and expose a small public API for 'getSnapshot()'.

2026-01-19 - Lena Thompson: Updated Figma to add micro-summary expanded state; added copy for screen-reader summary templates. Marked UX decision: default snapshot interval = 1000ms for battery-sensitive devices, 200ms on desktop. Linked specs: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/compact-micro-summary-v2
2026-01-26 - Design review: PM (Sofia Li) requested that the snapshot include a 'confidence' tag when downsampling or using aggregated values. Added requirement to engineering_notes.

2026-01-30 - ENG PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/feature/micro-summary (WIP). Perf dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abilities/micro-summary - early numbers: median cpu dropped 12%, dom nodes -42% under synthetic workload. Needs end-to-end a11y tests.

2026-02-02 - Accessibility audit (indie-a11y): Passed keyboard flow tests. Screen-reader snapshot content needs clearer separators between series; updated aria templates. Next: finalize copy and add tooltip variants for keyboard users.
